messages:
Anita R.: heads up — we saw a sharp GPU saturation spike in us-west-2 at ~18:04 UTC during the consumer batch window. queue depth jumped, p50 latency doubled, and a bunch of requests hit admission=reject.
Mike S.: ugh. saw the alerts. looks like multiple tenants ramped at once. warm-pool filled, but provisioning lagged ~40s on average.
Sofia P.: confirming. cluster metrics: pod startup tail latency went to 60s. autoscaler started 90s after queueing spike. :grimacing:
infra-bot: autoscaler event: scale_up triggered (target_pods +12) at 1854321998. warm-pool exhausted in pool-gpu-a.
Leo T.: quick notes: we have two overlapping issues — (A) too many simultaneous cold starts + (B) admission control aggressively rejects when queue > X. combined they create a feedback loop.
Anita R.: right. proposal: 1) stagger warm-pool activation to avoid synchronized starts, 2) implement deferred admission tokens (soft-queue) so we accept more but mark request as "deferred" and prioritize hedged routing, 3) add short-term predictive prewarm for expected bursty tenants.
Mike S.: for (1) i suggest we add jitter to warm-pool node spin-up timers and cap concurrent init at pool level. pseudo-config:

```
warmPool:
  target: 20
  initConcurrency: 3  # max nodes that can be spun up simultaneously
  initJitterMs: 15000
  scaleHysteresisSec: 45
```

this should smooth the spike on cloud API throttles and kube scheduling.
Sofia P.: (2) deferred admission sounds good. idea: hand out short-lived admission tokens per-tenant. token consumption doesn't block request but sets TTL and low-priority queue. fallback routes to replicas in different region or cheaper model.
Leo T.: admission-token config sketch:

```
admission:
  tokenWindow: 60s
  maxTokensPerTenant: 40
  softRejectThreshold: 0.85  # occupancy fraction to start deferring
  deferralTtlSec: 12
```

Mike S.: deferral approach reduces hard rejects but increases tail latency — need per-API SLO guardrails and observability in Redwood Console to surface deferred count vs hard rejects.
Anita R.: also want to avoid cost blowouts. predictive prewarm should use a short horizon model (5–10 min) based on recent request-rate slope, not absolute rate. if predicted spike > threshold, prewarm N nodes evenly spaced.
Sofia P.: i can add a simple slope-based predictor: if rate increase > 30% over 2mins, prewarm up to X nodes with linear ramp.
Leo T.: operational concerns: sticky pod provisioning (keep warm node assigned to same tenant for a while) reduces KV cache misses but increases fragmentation. we should measure unit-cost delta.
Anita R.: action items:
- Sofia: prototype jittered warm-pool init and add initConcurrency knob (PR + smoke test) — target EOD tomorrow.
- Mike: add admission-token prototype and metrics (deferred_count, token_usage) to /infra/metrics dash.
- Leo: run cost simulation for sticky vs pooled warm nodes, include cache-hit delta.

Mike S.: one more: add smoothing backoff to admission limiter to avoid step function. use exponential backoff with randomized jitter for re-admit attempts.

```
rateLimiter:
  baseWindowMs: 200
  backoffFactor: 1.6
  jitterPct: 0.25
```

Anita R.: + please add a small canary in us-west-2 tomorrow during the evening batch. will watch token usage and p99 latencies. if deferral reduces rejects without p99 > 3x, we roll.
Sofia P.: noted. i'll add a deploy flag and a deploy-bot canary annotation.
infra-bot: canary-deploy queued for us-west-2 at 1854322500, rollout strategy=staggered-5%
Mike S.: thanks — will monitor Logs and traces. will post short summary in this thread after canary.
Leo T.: also record cost delta from prewarm (cloud API hours) separately so product can weigh tradeoff.
Anita R.: cool. let's keep this tight. if anyone sees abnormal rejects or rising error rates after changes, ping here immediately. :thumbsup:
